scenes.headline: Where the bytes go in a small ternary model
scenes.sub: Bonsai 2 at 2B, 4B and 9B, read from the GGUF files.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ferrule! Bonsai 2 now comes in two, four and nine billion parameters. Here's where the bytes go when a ternary model gets small.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.text: Every matrix is still ternary, but at 2B the vocabulary table alone is 27% of the model, and the fixed costs start to show.
scenes.say: Every weight matrix is still minus one, zero or plus one. But at two billion, the vocabulary table alone is over a quarter of the model.

steps.say: The transformer blocks are about seventy percent of the file, packed five trits to a byte.
The vocabulary table is a quarter of it. It doubles as the output head, so every token reads it in full.
Norms and the state path stay in full precision, and the tokenizer rides in the header. Neither shrinks with the model.
That's why the small files land above the format's one point seven five bits per weight.

left.title: PQ2_0: 2.42 GB
left.say: The nine billion model ships twice. One pack gives each trit a two-bit slot: two point four two gigabytes, the repost's number.

right.title: PTQ1_0: 2.0 GB
right.say: The other packs five trits to a byte: two gigabytes, the number in the launch post. Same weights, different layout.

scenes.title: Why small means fast
scenes.say: Decoding one token at a time is a memory problem.

parts.note: every matrix is read once per token
parts.say: Each token streams every weight matrix once.

parts.note: how fast the chip can read memory
parts.say: So speed is just how fast the chip reads memory.

parts.note: a flat GB/s across sizes means bandwidth-bound
parts.say: Tokens per second times bytes gives the bandwidth a phone really used.

scenes.title: 9B decode on two iPhones
scenes.note: the iPhone 18 figure has no published method
scenes.say: The whitepaper measured an iPhone seventeen. The launch post quotes an iPhone eighteen, faster than the bandwidth math expects, with no method behind it.

scenes.text: At small sizes, the vocabulary and the packing decide the file, not the trits.
scenes.say: So at small sizes, the vocabulary and the packing decide the file size, not the trits.

recap: Decode speed is bytes per token
scenes.say: To recap: a big vocabulary, two packings of the same weights, and speed set by bytes per token.
